c.tagline: Korea's ancient Silla capital — royal tombs, stone temples and a thousand years of history in the open air.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are standard and honest; hailing through the Kakao T app is easiest since few drivers speak English. Base fares are low but the KTX station and Bulguksa are far enough out to add up.

emergency.note: 112 reaches police and 119 covers fire and ambulance; both have English-language assistance.

hood_desc: The walkable heart of old Gyeongju around Daereungwon (Tumuli Park), Cheomseongdae observatory, and the Gyeongju National Museum; grassy royal burial mounds sit between the streets and everything lights up at dusk. Best for first-timers who want the Silla sights on foot.

A trendy cafe-and-boutique street beside the tomb park lined with modern coffee houses, dessert shops, hanok-style eateries and local art; the city's liveliest evening strip and a favorite for younger travelers.

A landscaped lakeside resort district a few kilometers east with international hotels, a golf course, cherry-blossom paths and cruise boats; calm, green and family-friendly, though a short drive from the historic core.

The forested temple area on the slopes of Tohamsan, home to UNESCO-listed Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto; staying here means quiet mountain surroundings and early temple access before the tour buses arrive.
The downtown grid around Seongdong Market and the bus terminal, packed with traditional-market stalls, cheap eats and everyday shops; a convenient, budget-friendly and authentically local base.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though most Koreans prefer bottled or filtered.

transit.hours: City and intercity buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:30 PM; there is no metro or tram, so taxis and ride apps cover late nights.
transit.note: Gyeongju has no subway; travel is by local city bus, sightseeing bus routes linking the main sites, and taxis. The KTX high-speed train stops at Singyeongju Station outside town.
transit.pay: Tap a T-money or Cashbee transit card (sold at convenience stores) on boarding, or pay cash to the driver (around W1,500 per ride). The same card works nationwide.

bus: Intercity/express buses to Busan, Seoul, Daegu and beyond
train: KTX high-speed rail via Singyeongju Station (Seoul in ~2h)
Mugunghwa/ITX regional trains via Gyeongju Station

airport.name: Ulsan Airport (USN) — nearest; Gimhae Int'l (PUS) and Daegu (TAE) also serve the city

transit.m: KTX from Seoul to Singyeongju Station (~2h), then 15-min taxi (~W15,000) to the historic center
Frequent intercity bus from Busan (~1h) to Gyeongju Bus Terminal
Limousine bus or taxi from Ulsan Airport (~40 min)

tip.r: Not expected anywhere; service is included and rounding up is unnecessary.

food.name: Ssambap
food.desc: Rice and grilled or braised meat wrapped in leaf vegetables, served Gyeongju-style with twenty to thirty small side dishes.

places.name: Ssambap Street
places.note: Whole lane of ssambap houses beside the royal tombs; the local default for lunch.

places.name: Hankook Gwan
places.note: Long-running ssambap and bibimbap restaurant regularly named in Gyeongju guides.

places.name: Yosokkung
places.note: Upmarket hanok set-menu house serving the aristocratic version of the wrapped-rice table.

food.name: Hwangnam-ppang
food.desc: Palm-sized bun with a paper-thin skin packed almost entirely with red-bean paste, baked in Gyeongju since 1939.

places.name: Hwangnam Bread main shop
places.note: The original bakery; you can watch them filled and stamped through the window.

places.name: Hwangnam-dong shop cluster
places.note: Several licensed outlets around the tomb park sell them warm by the box.

places.name: Singyeongju KTX Station shops
places.note: Handy last stop to buy boxes before the train home.

food.name: Chalboribbang
food.desc: Flat, chewy glutinous-barley cake pressed around sweet red bean; nuttier and less sugary than Hwangnam bread.

places.name: Chalboribbang shops on Poseok-ro
places.note: Cluster of barley-cake bakeries near the tombs, most baking through the day.

places.name: Gyeongju Jungang Market
places.note: Market stalls sell them loose and cheaper than the tourist-strip shops.

places.name: Bomun Lake resort shops
places.note: Convenient for anyone staying by the lake rather than in the old town.

food.name: Boribap jeongsik
food.desc: Barley rice mixed at the table with mountain greens, soybean paste and stew, a farm-style meal tied to Gyeongju's barley country.

places.name: Restaurants below Bulguksa
places.note: Temple-approach eateries serve barley-rice sets with heaps of seasoned greens.

places.name: Samneung trailhead restaurants
places.note: Hikers' spot for barley rice and doenjang stew after the Namsan Buddha trails.

places.name: Gyeongju Jungang Market
places.note: Market food alley does cheap barley-rice sets alongside soup and noodles.

food.name: Gampo seafood and mulhoe
food.desc: East-coast catch from Gyeongju's own port: raw fish, steamed crab and mulhoe, cold raw fish in a chilled sweet-spicy broth.

places.name: Gampo Port fish market
places.note: Buy from the stalls and have it served upstairs; busiest at weekends.

places.name: Bonggil Beach restaurant row
places.note: Seafront strip near the underwater tomb of King Munmu, good for grilled fish.

places.name: Gyeongju Jungang Market
places.note: In-town option if you are not driving out to the coast.

food.name: Gyeongju gyodong beopju
food.desc: Clear amber rice wine brewed by the Choi family of Gyo-dong for centuries and designated an intangible cultural asset.

places.name: Gyodong Beopju house
places.note: Brewed at the Choi family compound in the hanok village where it originated.

places.name: Yosokkung
places.note: Serves beopju with its traditional set courses, the intended pairing.

places.name: Gyeongju Jungang Market
places.note: Bottles sold alongside other regional liquors if the brewery is closed.

food.name: Sikhye
food.desc: Sweet cloudy rice punch scented with malt and served ice cold, the standard palate-cleanser after a heavy ssambap table.

places.name: Gyeongju Jungang Market
places.note: Stalls ladle it from chilled tubs; cheapest and most local version.

places.name: Hwangnam-dong cafes
places.note: Tea houses along the tomb-park lanes pour sikhye alongside traditional teas.

places.name: Ssambap Street restaurants
places.note: Most ssambap houses finish the meal with a glass of sikhye.

landmarks: Bulguksa Temple
The crown jewel of Silla Buddhism, this UNESCO-listed 8th-century temple dazzles with twin stone pagodas, graceful staircases and hillside pavilions wrapped in maple forest.
Seokguram Grotto
High on Mount Toham, a serene granite Buddha gazes toward the East Sea from an ingenious domed grotto, considered East Asia's finest Buddhist sculpture.
Daereungwon Tomb Complex (Cheonmachong)
Grass-covered burial mounds of Silla kings swell across central Gyeongju like green hills, with the Heavenly Horse Tomb open to reveal golden crowns and treasures.
Cheomseongdae Observatory
This bottle-shaped 7th-century stone tower is Asia's oldest surviving astronomical observatory, an elegant testament to Silla science glowing beautifully under evening lights.
Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond (Anapji)
Reflected pavilions of a Silla royal pleasure garden shimmer across this lotus pond at dusk, delivering Gyeongju's most magical nighttime photograph.
Gyeongju National Museum
Golden crowns, the massive Divine Bell of King Seongdeok and thousands of Silla treasures make this Korea's essential archaeology museum, set amid landscaped grounds.
Woljeonggyo Bridge
A sumptuously reconstructed Silla-era covered wooden bridge spans the Namcheon stream, its lantern-lit galleries and reflections drawing photographers every evening.
Hwangnidan-gil Street
Hanok houses converted into stylish cafés, dessert shops and boutiques line this trendy lane between royal tombs, where visitors stroll in rented hanbok.
Namsan Mountain
An open-air museum of Silla devotion, this sacred mountain's trails pass hundreds of Buddha reliefs, pagodas and shrine ruins carved directly into granite outcrops.
Yangdong Folk Village
A UNESCO-listed Joseon clan village of tiled aristocratic manors and thatched cottages spills down wooded hillsides, still inhabited after more than 500 years.

train.note: High-speed trains use the station on the Gyeongbu high-speed line about 15 minutes west of the centre - opened as Singyeongju and now signed simply as Gyeongju - and both Korail's KTX from Seoul Station and SRT from Suseo call there, taking around two hours from the capital. The old city-centre Gyeongju station closed to passengers at the end of December 2021 when the Donghae Line was rerouted, so do not aim for it. Reservations open about a month ahead and sell out around Chuseok and Lunar New Year; foreign visitors can also use the Korail Pass. There is no international train from South Korea - the line north across the DMZ carries no passengers.

bus.note: The express and intercity bus terminals sit next to each other near the Hwangnam area, walkable from the main sights and much closer to town than the KTX station. Buses from the Seoul Express Bus Terminal leave roughly every 40 minutes and take about four hours, while Busan, Daegu and Pohang services run at least every 20 minutes and take 40 minutes to an hour; there are also direct limousine coaches from Gimhae and Incheon airports. Book express services at Kobus (https://www.kobus.co.kr/) and intercity ones at Bustago (https://www.bustago.or.kr/), or pay at the terminal machines. South Korea has no international bus routes.

ferry.note: Gyeongju has no passenger ferry terminal - the historic sites are inland and the small stretch of coast at Gampo is a fishing harbour. The nearest sailings are from Pohang, about an hour northeast, for the Ulleungdo island ferries, and from Busan, roughly 90 minutes south, whose International Passenger Terminal serves Fukuoka, Shimonoseki and Osaka.

half.name: Busan
half.blurb: South Korea's second-largest city, with Haeundae Beach, the Jagalchi fish market, and Gamcheon's terraced hillside houses.

half.name: Pohang
half.blurb: Steel-industry port city with the Homigot Sunrise Square and a coastline of unusual rock formations.

half.name: Andong Hahoe Folk Village
half.blurb: Riverside Joseon-era village of traditional tile and thatched houses, still lived in by descendants of the founding clan.

half.name: Ulsan
half.blurb: Industrial port city with the Taehwagang River bamboo forest and prehistoric Bangudae petroglyphs nearby.
